ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories against the consolidated UN Security Council sanctions list, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, and Canadian Criminal Code wire/unlawful activity standards. OFAC's SDN list is contractually required where USD correspondent banking or Swift_TT is used. PEP screening follows FINTRAC guidance and PCMLTFA requirements: enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs, heads of state, senior ministers, senior military, judiciary and politically exposed family/close associates. Source of funds and source of wealth verification is required for any PEPs and for transfers above internal threshold. The business activity of computerized embroidery and ultrasonic seaming of custom plush dolls is assessed as Low_Risk_Standard, but financial institutions and payment platforms may request documentary proof of commercial rationale, supply-chain transparency, and customs classification (HS 9503.00).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online enterprise registry and name clearance portal, accessible at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec corporate names must be in French under the Charter of the French Language. A name in another language may be registered only if accompanied by a French version or if it is a registered trademark benefit of an exemption. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin script under official romanization standards; the French version prevails for legal and regulatory purposes. The corporate designation must be a permitted Quebec form: 'Incorporée', 'Société par actions', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Corporation', 'Ltée', or equivalent French/English marker.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government of Canada / Gouvernement du Québec
Quebec / Québec as a standalone distinctive token without government authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ name rejection, the applicant may either file a revised name reservation request or request administrative review by the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal, stating legal and factual grounds and paying the statutory review fee. If the review confirms refusal, the applicant may apply for judicial review by the Court of Quebec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the Code of Civil Procedure. Where the name is refused because of an opposition filed by a third party, the applicant may negotiate withdrawal, amend the name, or seek a court declaration permitting registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for Quebec incorporation only if the virtual office provider acts as the registered office, is physically located in Quebec, accepts service of legal process during business hours, and maintains the statutory records. A virtual mailbox alone does not replace the registered office where directors' and accounting records are kept and to which Revenu Québec, Canada Revenue Agency, and process servers can have lawful access. For a plush toy OEM, production and warehousing may be located outside the registered office address, but the registered address must be a real, operable location in Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 8% in year 1, rising to 20% by year 3 from Revenu Québec, CRA, Health Canada, or Canada Border Services Agency. Border and Customs inspections are more likely for imported stuffed toys under the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act, S.C. 2010, c. 21, SOR/2011-17, but physical on-site inspection of the corporate registered office is less likely unless tax non-compliance, false address declaration, or product-safety complaints are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1 (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), ss. 9-40 (incorporation, articles, registered office, directors and officers); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, art. 88 (French corporate name and filing language).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Quebec Enterprise Registrar; central register of legal persons in Quebec; sole statutory online window for incorporation filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de constitution (Form A-1) / Articles of Incorporation under the QBCA, filed electronically through the REQ online services platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed; the board fixes the consideration (cash, property or services) for issued shares. No escrow or capital verification account is required for a domestic business corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Corporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, be hereby ratified and approved. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the offer to subscribe for 100 common shares at a subscription price of CAD 1.00 per share, fully paid, be accepted and the board authorizes issuance thereof. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at [street address], Montreal, Quebec, and the mailing address be designated. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the by-laws of the Corporation be adopted effective immediately, subject to shareholder ratification at the next annual meeting. FINALLY RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: President and Chief Executive Officer, Treasurer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until successors are elected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Optional Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online Services en ligne portal and name reservation service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Propose up to three distinct corporate names (French or bilingual; a numbered company may be used as alternative). Run a name search against the REQ central register and common-law trademark databases to verify distinctiveness; if a name is selected, file the REQ name-reservation request online, which reserves the name for 90 days. Ensure the French-language form requirement under the Charter of the French Language is respected.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names (list of at least 3 alternatives)
REQ online declaration for name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for lack of distinctiveness or public-order concerns, refile with alternative names within 30 days or request administrative reconsideration with justification; a numbered company may bypass the name requirement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - electronic filing of Form A-1.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the official Statuts de constitution form in French with: corporate name and name reservation reference (if any), full registered office address in Quebec, number or range of directors, authorized share structure (classes, par value, rights and transfer restrictions), and the incorporator's signature. Submit the application online with electronic signature and pay the statutory filing fee (CAD 337.10 online, inclusive of REQ registration and certificate duties). The incorporation is recorded simultaneously in the Registre des entreprises.
required_dossiers: Form A-1 - Statuts de constitution (Articles of Incorporation)
Certificate of name reservation (where a named company)
Proof of identity of incorporator/initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of incompleteness or legal defect, amend and resubmit the corrected form within the prescribed delay; repeated rejection triggers a written explanatory notice, after which administrative review by REQ may be sought.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Constitution and Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - certificates division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, retrieve the official Certificate of Constitution and the attributed ten-digit NEQ from the REQ online platform; verify the legal name, date of constitution and registered office data on the public register extract. Archive the certificate and register extract in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Official extract from the Registre des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where clerical errors appear in the certificate or register extract, file a correction request (Demande de correction) through REQ online services; minor corrections are processed without substantive re-review.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal corporate income tax and GST, portal: CRA My Business Account; Revenu Québec for Quebec corporate income tax and Quebec Sales Tax (QST), portal: Revenu Québec Mon dossier d'entreprise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain certificate of incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act; the corporate registry transmits basic entity data to CRA and Revenu Québec, but the taxpayer must activate the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and tax accounts. Step 2: Register the BN and the Corporation Income Tax account with CRA through Business Registration Online; register the GST account (RT program account) when taxable worldwide supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any four consecutive calendar quarters, or voluntarily to claim input tax credits. Step 3: For a business carrying on activities in Quebec, register with Revenu Québec for the QST and Quebec corporate tax accounts, obtaining the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and the QST registration number. Step 4: If the Canadian corporation is foreign-owned, the non-resident ownership rules do not restrict tax registration, but a non-resident corporation not incorporated in Canada may instead be required to obtain a CRA non-resident BN and, if it has a permanent establishment or Quebec business presence, a Revenu Québec QST registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope: A CBCA or QBCA business corporation is a separate taxable person resident in Canada; it is subject to federal Part I corporate tax and Quebec corporate tax on worldwide income, and no pass-through or tax-transparent treatment is available. A non-resident corporation not incorporated in Canada is taxable in Canada only on Canadian-source income and may be taxable in Quebec if it carries on business or has a permanent establishment in Quebec. The plush-toy OEM manufacturing activity is not located in a tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election and no elective pass-through exist in Canadian tax law. Ordinary corporate elections available include the s. 85(1) rollover on transferring property to the corporation, the s. 89(11) capital dividend account election, and the election by a non-resident corporation to compute Canadian-source business or rental income on a net basis under relevant provisions. Hybrid-mismatch elections are not available; Canada applies mandatory anti-hybrid rules and the excessive interest and financing expenses limitation (EIFEL) regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administered by Revenu Québec; combined value-added-style consumption tax regime for taxable tangible personal property in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: a person is a GST small supplier until total worldwide taxable supplies in a calendar quarter and the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters are CAD 30,000 or less; registration becomes mandatory once the threshold is exceeded. Quebec applies a parallel QST small-supplier threshold of CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Quebec. A plush-toy OEM supplying B2B goods into Canada or Quebec above the threshold must register and charge GST and QST unless the supply qualifies as a zero-rated export.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is no national real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or CRA invoice-clearance API in Canada. GST and QST invoices may be issued electronically in a readable format without CRA or Revenu Québec prior approval, provided they contain the prescribed information. Quebec has introduced an electronic-invoicing framework for QST registrants using structured e-invoices and XML/EDI formats; however no transaction-level clearance or digital stamp is currently operative. Suppliers must maintain invoice records in CRA and Revenu Québec acceptable electronic form for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST and QST are zero-rated on exports of tangible personal property exported from Canada as soon as reasonably possible after transfer of possession, including plush mascot dolls shipped by courier or freight to foreign buyers, provided the goods are not consumed or used in Canada before export. Contract manufacturing, embroidery, sewing, and ultrasonic seaming services performed in Canada on goods that are subsequently exported may also qualify for zero-rating where the evidence identifies the foreign recipient and the actual export movement. For separately supplied services to non-residents, zero-rating generally requires that the service be supplied to a non-resident and not be performed in connection with Canadian real estate or goods consumed in Canada. Because zero-rated exports are taxable supplies, the exporter may claim input tax credits and input tax refunds on inputs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A / Canadian Export Reporting System e-manifest record) for shipments exceeding CAD 2,000 or controlled goods
Commercial invoice and signed purchase order identifying the plush toy HS code 9503.00 and NAICS 339930
Bill of lading, air waybill, or courier consignment note showing Canadian origin and foreign destination
Packing list and certificate of origin where preferential tariff treatment is claimed
Proof of export delivery, such as carrier receipt, terminal receipt, or foreign customs entry evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank inward-remittance advice tying foreign-currency export proceeds to the invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess and claw back zero-rating and related input tax credits or refunds where export documentation is incomplete or inconsistent with the invoice. The normal reassessment period is four years, extended to seven years for misrepresentation, with no limitation period in cases of fraud. False or grossly negligent export zero-rating claims may attract federal gross-negligence false-statement penalties under the Excise Tax Act, equivalent Quebec penalties, interest, and criminal tax-evasion prosecution with substantial fines and imprisonment. Export proceeds should be repatriated and matched to invoices within 180 days to support the evidentiary file and avoid heightened audit scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — monetary authority and lender of last resort; prudential banking regulation is administered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act (Canada); anti-money-laundering supervision is exercised by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) pursuant to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; Quebec-level provincial financial-sector conduct and non-bank deposit-taking oversight is vested in the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). Canada operates an open, liberalized FX regime with no statutory exchange-control authority requiring pre-authorization of cross-border capital movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions; Canada has accepted Article VIII obligations under the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no quantitative limits, permit systems, or central-bank approval gates on dividend distributions, royalty payments, interest remittances, management fees, or loan principal repayments to non-residents. Profit-remittance hurdles are purely fiscal: a non-resident shareholder of a Quebec Business Corporation faces withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) at a 25% statutory rate, generally reduced to 10% on dividends under the Canada–China income tax treaty, and to 15% on arm's-length interest or royalties where the treaty applies; Quebec does not impose a separate provincial withholding on non-resident dividend remittances. Remittance mechanics require the corporation to file an NR4 information return with Canada Revenue Agency, remit the withheld amount electronically, and provide the payee with an NR4 slip; no exchange-control release certificate or CAD conversion authorization is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory statutory conversion ratio; a Canadian exporter may lawfully retain USD or other foreign currency in a foreign-currency bank account or convert to CAD at its sole discretion. The only binding reporting duties are: (i) presentation of a B13A Export Declaration to the Canada Border Services Agency for commercial exports by air, sea, rail, or land where the shipment value exceeds CAD 2,000, and (ii) statistical reporting of export payments for Statistics Canada balance-of-payments purposes — such reporting is purely informational and does not constitute a control or surrender mechanism. Under PCMLTFA, corporate records must preserve proof of export payments for five years; the deposit of any export proceeds in a Canadian CDIC-member institution is protected only up to CAD 100,000 per insured category.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for ancillary payment aggregation and marketplace settlement; Low for deposit-taking, documentary credits, or sole treasury sovereignty. A foreign digital EMI such as Wise, Payoneer, or Stripe may lawfully onboard a Quebec Business Corporation as a payment service provider without a Canadian bank charter, receiving inbound receipts and distributing outbound supplier disbursements. However, a foreign EMI cannot accept deposits in the legal sense, cannot issue cheques, and cannot provide domestic Canadian payment accounts unless registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), effective September 2024, which requires payment service providers with incidental Canadian activity to register with the Bank of Canada; an EMI offering money remittance must also register with FINTRAC as a money services business. The optimal treasury structure is a Tier-1 Canadian DDA as master treasury account, with Platform_Pay (including PayPal and Payoneer) subledgers for marketplace receipts swept daily to the operational account via SWIFT or EFT; EMIs alone cannot support commercial letters of credit or documentary collection settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Quebec Business Corporation with non-resident directors or shareholders, PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance permit remote customer identification where verification is performed using an 'authorized verification method' — including a real-time electronic identity verification portal or an attestation by a prescribed FINTRAC-reporting entity, such as an existing Canadian bank, credit union, or trust company. In operational practice, the Big-6 chartered banks in Quebec require at least one director or authorized officer to present an original passport and proof of residential address during a live video interview, or to attend in person at a Quebec branch for the initial account subscription. A face-to-face interview becomes a hard internal mandate when: (i) no director is resident in Canada; (ii) the controlling shareholder resides in a high-risk jurisdiction; (iii) the forecast annual turnover exceeds CAD 5 million; or (iv) the account is requested to open simultaneously with a commercial letter-of-credit facility. Where a fully remote opening is attempted, the bank will demand notarized corporate documents, a Quebec-registered physical address that is not merely a mail-forwarding drop, and a legal-opinion letter from a Canadian attorney or a Quebec notary confirming the authority of the signing officers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is resident in the People's Republic of China or Hong Kong and controls 25% or more of voting equity with no Canadian-resident director; this triggers enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered articles of incorporation and certificate of corporate status from Corporations Canada or Registraire des entreprises du Québec; certified corporate share register; notarized passport copies and proof of address for every UBO holding 25% or more; notarized Chinese or Hong Kong corporate registry extracts with apostille/legalization; a 12-month bank statement history of the parent company; signed OEM manufacturing contracts evidencing genuine commercial activity; and a written source-of-funds letter from a licensed Canadian CPA confirming the equity capital corresponds to real export-trade earnings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical office in Quebec; registered office is a professional agent's address, and all directors are non-resident, giving rise to a 'brass-plate company' red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or sublease agreement in the corporate name; CPA of Quebec confirmation of active business substance; utility and operating-expense invoices at a Quebec address; customs and transport waybills showing physical movement of stuffed toys and plush fabrics; Quebec warehouse or fulfillment centre agreement; and a board-minute resolution documenting the intended staffing plan for embroidery and ultrasonic seaming operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound equity injection from the PRC/HK parent exceeding CAD 100,000 within the first 30 days of account opening, a pattern frequently associated with layering and round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed equity subscription agreement; issued share certificate; directors' resolution authorizing the capital call; paid-up capital schedule reconciling to the bank transfer; CRA T2 corporate information return schedules; the parent company's audited financial statements; a board-approved treasury map demonstrating the injection funds specific machinery purchases (computerized embroidery and ultrasonic sewing equipment); and a sworn statutory declaration by an authorized officer confirming that no third-party funds are intermingled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering pattern indicators: receipts from Chinese and Hong Kong platform counterparties paired with outbound disbursements to Asian apparel and fabric suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete purchase-order chain, commercial invoices, bills of lading, and customs entry/export documents; letters of assurance from contracted suppliers confirming the physical delivery of raw textiles, fill materials, and accessories; a transaction map correlating each inbound payment to a specific order and each outbound payment to a specific supplier invoice; historical settlement records from payment gateways; and an independent annual AML/ATF self-review aligned to FINTRAC Trade-Based Money Laundering indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list or adverse-media hits against a proposed director due to name-match false positives common with Chinese transliterations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Professionally generated enhanced due-diligence report from a reputable compliance database; beneficial-ownership chart showing the named individual holds no sanctioned entity positions; notarized affidavit explaining the media finding or denying association; legal confirmation that the individual is not a politically exposed person; and, where the bank remains unsatisfied, a board resolution removing the implicated director and appointing a Canadian-resident independent director to restore onboarding viability.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The equity injection from the non-resident shareholder to the Quebec Business Corporation is executed via SWIFT MT103 in CAD or USD from the parent bank to the designated Capital Escrow sub-account at the Canadian Tier-1 bank. Canada does not maintain the Chinese-style state-administration purpose-code registry; however, the remittance narrative must be precise: 'Share subscription — paid-in capital contribution under the Business Corporations Act (Canada)' or the institution-specific 'Equity Investment' reason code. The compliance verification bundle comprises: directors' resolution authorizing the share issuance; executed subscription agreement; share certificate registered in the corporate minute book; updated Quebec Registraire des entreprises declaration; and the escrow ledger record. Upon completion of the minute book, treasury moves funds from the escrow sub-account to the operational account by an internal journal entry, and the contribution is characterized as paid-up capital for Income Tax Act purposes; if the parent finances via shareholder loan instead, the transaction must respect thin-capitalization rules of subsection 78(4?) (strictly the ratio-based subparagraph 18(4)?) and Part XIII withholding on any interest. The bank performs a source-of-funds verification for every inward transfer above CAD 10,000 and records the transaction under FINTRAC wire-transfer recordkeeping for amounts exceeding CAD 1,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement to Chinese OEM fabric, stuffing, and embroidery suppliers follows a dual rail structure: (i) for high-value or first-time transactions, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by a Canadian chartered bank under UCP600, advised and confirmed by the beneficiary's bank in China; and (ii) for repeat open-account trade, SWIFT MT103 wire transfers routed through Payments Canada's Lynx high-value payment system with final settlement, including field 70 remittance information referencing the purchase order and invoice. Low-value sample orders and marketplace payouts are cleared through Platform_Pay rails (PayPal or Payoneer), with daily automated sweeps to the primary DDA to avoid trapped balances. Each disbursement must be matched to an approved purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list, and either a bill of lading or a courier waybill for the plush goods; no regulatory pre-clearance is required under Canadian law, but the treasury must preserve full originator and beneficiary data for five years under PCMLTFA cross-border wire-transfer recordkeeping rules applicable to transactions above CAD 1,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CAD outright forward contracts (tenor up to 24 months) concluded with an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank under an ISDA 2020 French? master agreement or bank standard treasury terms
USD/CAD FX swaps combining a spot transaction with a simultaneous forward reversal for short-term working-capital management
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for converting USD-denominated trade-payable exposures into CAD obligations
Plain-vanilla European-style USD/CAD currency options purchased to cap adverse conversion risk while retaining upside benefit

CNY/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted with a major Canadian bank for hedging the Chinese supply-chain cost base; NDFs are not offered for CAD because CAD is fully convertible with a deep onshore forward market, and any NDF arrangement must be documented as a trade-related hedge transaction within the bank's internal risk appetite

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Quebec Enterprise Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the enterprise registration (or of the last annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of CAD 200 (approx. USD 148); registration may be revoked after one year of continuous default, preceded by a notice of intention and a 60-day rectification period; directors may be personally exposed on persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal annual return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (applicable where the corporation is CBCA-incorporated; not required for a purely provincial QBCA corporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary late fee; failure to file for at least one year exposes the corporation to administrative dissolution under section 212 CBCA, with a notice of intention to dissolve followed by strike-off if not cured within 90 days; revival is possible within 5 years upon filing all arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the register of individuals with significant control (RPCI / UBO register) and reporting in the annual declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), with source records maintained in the company's statutory register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the Quebec annual declaration within 60 days of the registration anniversary; any material change (for example, a transfer of a 25% or more interest) must be entered in the register within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties for false or omitted declarations: CAD 1,000–10,000 for individual officers and CAD 5,000–50,000 for corporations; REQ may also refuse or revoke enterprise registration for repeated default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, asset, or headcount threshold imposes a mandatory audit for a private Quebec business corporation; audit appointment may be waived by unanimous shareholder resolution (section 163 CBCA / Article 208 QBCA). A compulsory independent audit applies only to distributing public-offering corporations, corporations with listed securities, and corporations whose shareholders validly demand audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook) for public enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) for private corporations; tax-basis statements consistent with the Income Tax Act (Canada) for CRA and Revenu Québec filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Since June 30, 2024, every QBCA corporation must create and maintain a register of individuals with significant control (individuals holding 25% or more of voting rights, 25% or more of equity value, or exercising de facto control). Information must be refreshed with the annual REQ declaration and updated within 30 days of any share transfer or change in control; CBCA corporations are concurrently subject to the federal significant-control register rules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholders' and directors' minutes of meetings)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (Quebec RPCI, effective June 30, 2024)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–800 per year for a Quebec registered office address, registered agent services, and corporate secretarial support including annual declaration preparation and UBO register maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–6,500 for a CPA Canada audit of a small private manufacturing corporation; USD 800–2,000 for a review engagement when the audit is waived by unanimous shareholder resolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined statutory headline rate (15% federal Part I plus 11.5% Quebec corporate income tax), before small business and manufacturing reductions
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction: 9% federal and 3.2% Quebec rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable investment tax credit of up to 35% for eligible CCPCs; Quebec research and development tax credit; Manufacturing and Processing tax credit and provincial equipment investment credits for plush-toy OEM facilities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; electronically filed through CRA EFILE / GENIENT or approved commercial tax software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; taxation year cannot exceed 53 weeks
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the corporation's taxation year-end; final federal tax balance generally due within 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible CCPCs); large corporations must remit monthly instalments

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period end date — calendar date closing the taxation year; must match the audited financial statements and Quebec CO-17 return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must report the Canadian fiscal period end used for the branch permanent establishment accounting records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Canadian Business Number (BN/RC programme account) for the corporation; identifies the Part I corporate account with the CRA
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must obtain a BN before filing and designate a Canadian resident agent or permanent establishment address on the return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income — net income after reserves, losses, prior-year loss carryovers and applicable adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation reports only taxable income earned through a Canadian permanent establishment, using the Part I and Quebec allocation rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Part I tax before credits — base federal corporate tax at 15%, reduced for CCPC small business rates and manufacturing deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations do not claim the CCPC Small Business Deduction and compute Part I tax at the general federal rate on allocated Canadian source income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxes payable after applying refundable/non-refundable credits such as SR&ED, investment tax credits, foreign tax credits and provincial attribution
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim only treaty and Canadian statutory credits attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment; no SBD or provincial manufacturing credits are available

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under Income Tax Act s.162(1): 5% of unpaid federal tax plus 1% per full month late up to 12 months; repeated failure attracts 10% plus 2% per month; failure to remit source withholdings attracts 10%-20% additional penalty and prescribed daily interest; gross negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed via Revenu Québec's Cliquez/EDIfile electronic services
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned with the federal T2 taxation year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed within 6 months after fiscal year-end and Quebec tax balance must be remitted by the same deadline; eligible CCPCs generally receive a 3-month extension for the final balance only

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation identification and Quebec establishment — legal name, head office address, Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), permanent establishment address and directors' names
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation must identify the Quebec permanent establishment, its address and the designated Quebec representative; no NEQ is issued to extra-provincial corporations carrying on business dependently

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income earned in Quebec — income attributable under the Taxation Act allocation formula applied to taxable income earned from the permanent establishment in Quebec
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident computes Quebec allocation on the same basis as federal permanent establishment allocation; non-Quebec Canadian income is excluded

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after deducting loss carryovers and reserves allowed under the Quebec Taxation Act
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Quebec-based losses from the permanent establishment may be deducted; home-jurisdiction losses are not admissible

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec tax before credits — 11.5% general corporate rate, subject to the Quebec Small Business Deduction at 3.2% for eligible active business income up to CAD 500,000
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation is ineligible for the Quebec SBD and is taxed at the full 11.5% rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on capital for financial institutions; generally nil for plush toy OEM corporations not classified as financial institutions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident treaty-protected financial institutions must still compute the tax capital base if they hold Canadian investment properties; otherwise leave blank

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid Quebec tax plus 1% per full month late up to 12 months; prescribed interest and penalties on repeated non-filing; false statement penalty of 50% of resulting understatement; document production penalties of CAD 500 per day for failure to provide transfer pricing information

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 40% combined domestic statutory withholding on dividends paid to non-residents (25% federal Part XIII withholding tax plus 15% Quebec special dividend tax), subject to reduction under an applicable tax treaty (generally 5% for corporate controlling shareholders and 15% for portfolio shareholders)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must deliver to the paying corporation (i) a completed CRA Form NR301 (or equivalent federal treaty application) requesting reduced Part XIII withholding, (ii) a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty partner tax authority, and (iii) for Quebec purposes, the equivalent Revenu Québec declaration establishing treaty entitlement; the payer must keep the certificate on file and may apply the treaty rate only if the protocol is satisfied before the dividend remittance; if overwithheld, the non-resident files CRA Form NR7 / Quebec refund application
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Part XIII withholding: 25% on royalties for use of IP (trademarks, character copyright, industrial drawings) and 25% on interest not subject to domestic exemption; treaty-reduced royalty rates under Canada-US DTA are generally 0% for copyright royalties and 10% for industrial/patent royalties; interest paid to an arm's-length non-resident lender on non-participating debt is generally exempt from Canadian withholding under s.212(3); Quebec does not impose a separate 15% provincial tax on interest or royalties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 annual aggregate fair market value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions (Form T106 threshold); corporations above this threshold are required to maintain contemporaneous Local File/transfer pricing documentation to preserve 'reasonable efforts' defence against penalties and to substantiate Master File data under CRA/OECD guidance
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute; instead, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245 and Quebec Taxation Act s.1079.5.1) applies and requires genuine commercial substance. For a plush-toy OEM, economic substance evidence includes actual employees, physical factory premises, inventory risk, equipment, management decision-making, and real OEM customer contracts; absence of these factors triggers GAAR recharacterization, denial of intercompany payments, and in severe cases treaty-shopping or sham arguments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Conscious Omission in Corporate Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting taxable income by omitting cash sales, online platform revenue, export sales, royalties from licensed mascot characters, or off-book recovery of tooling costs from OEM customers in Quebec or federal filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.239(1): conviction for tax evasion carries a fine of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; Quebec Taxation Act imposes a 50% civil penalty for wilful false statements; CRA may reassess beyond the normal 3-year limitation period where misrepresentation is involved; interest and penalties accumulate daily.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause false returns to be filed are personally exposed to criminal prosecution, personal fines, restitution orders and imprisonment up to 5 years; travel bans are commonly attached as bail conditions in cross-border tax prosecutions; if the corporation is found to be a sham or a façade, courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for the corporation's tax, penalties and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Unjustified Margin Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling plush mascot inventory to a related foreign distributor at a negative margin or below arm's length CUP while booking inflated management fees, fabric costs or trademark royalties to a low-tax related entity, without a contemporaneous transfer pricing study or Form T106 filing for cross-border transactions in excess of CAD 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing penalty under ITA s.247(3) of 10% of the net upward TP adjustment; failure to file T106 incurs CAD 100 per day, maximum CAD 2,500; false statement gross negligence penalty under s.163.2 is 50% of the understated tax; extended reassessment period of 6 years for TP adjustments; Quebec parallel TP rules and penalties apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for transfer pricing penalties, but if directors sign false declarations or knowingly instruct intercompany pricing based on fabricated terms, they face civil restitution and gross-negligence penalties; knowing participation in a transfer-pricing sham may support criminal prosecution under s.239 and director exposure to the 100%-200% evasion penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Quebec corporation merely as an invoicing vehicle while actual production, inventory, staffing, and risk management are located in a non-treaty or low-tax jurisdiction, with profits artificially diverted through service agreements or cost-plus arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR allows the CRA and Revenu Québec to disallow the entire tax benefit and recharacterize the arrangement; offshore investment entity rules under ITA s.94 may deem certain foreign property income accrued; Part XIII withholding may be imposed on deemed dividends or management fees; false offshore reporting can trigger criminal tax evasion charges; corporate and provincial penalties can exceed 50% of the avoided tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the shell structure is a deliberate sham or a sham used to defeat creditors, courts will pierce the corporate veil under the Fenmount standard; directors become jointly and severally liable for corporate taxes, interest, penalties and restitution; laundering benefits through shell invoicing invites offences under Criminal Code s.462.31 with imprisonment up to 10 years and asset forfeiture.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Proceeds of Crime Integration through OEM Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring customer settlements through Swift_TT and Platform_Pay in a way that disguises true beneficiaries, splits invoices to conceal related-party transactions, or uses shell recipients to accept or refund payments for non-existent licensing or tooling services; failing to register with FINTRAC if the business acts as a money services business or conducts occasional large cash transactions for third parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act administrative penalties can reach CAD 1,000,000 per contravention for corporations; Criminal Code s.462.31 authorizes imprisonment up to 10 years for laundering proceeds of crime; criminal forfeiture of property under s.462.37; direct fines under controlled substances statutes when applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who organize, instruct or participate in laundering transactions are personally subject to arrest, pre-trial travel bans, freezing orders, asset seizure, criminal fines and imprisonment up to 10 years; convictions may lead to disqualification from serving as directors under federal or Quebec corporate legislation and to civil restitution to victims and tax authorities.
